title: Continuing a useful result
opening: A drill still helps other players, but its creator no longer wants to maintain it every day. Decide whether the result should continue, then separate that decision from who can actually carry it.

labels.comparison: Compare ways the drill could stay useful
labels.comparisonIntro: The same result can take different forms. Compare the added benefit with the work and obligations each form creates.

forms.label: Recommend an existing resource
forms.description: Use when an available drill already fits the players and conditions.
forms.benefit: Players can reach a useful drill without creating a duplicate.
forms.burden: Check that the resource still fits; the original creator does not inherit its maintenance.
forms.mustBeTrue: The resource is available to the intended players and fits their situation.

forms.label: Share the current drill
forms.description: Keep the current version available to the people who can use it.
forms.benefit: Players retain access to a result that already helps.
forms.burden: Access alone does not provide correction, maintenance, or a responsible operator.
forms.mustBeTrue: The intended users can access the drill, and its present limits are clear.

forms.label: Run a supported service
forms.description: Consider this when people need ongoing feedback or implementation help.
forms.benefit: A service can provide continuing support around the drill.
forms.burden: It adds delivery, staffing, funding, exchange, and maintenance obligations.
forms.mustBeTrue: An actual operator, resources, delivery route, and economics can support the promise. Usefulness alone does not establish a business.

labels.sequence: Follow the seven parts in order. New use, corrections, failures, or changed conditions can send the next review back to an earlier part.
labels.sourceQuote: When a finding, method or creation may deserve continued use: 1. Establish what is supported and whose situation it can help. 2. Research existing ways to make it available and people who could maintain it. 3. Compare the added benefit and total burden of those forms. 4. Examine exchange and economics if a commercial arrangement is proposed. 5. Choose what to do: retain, share, recommend, improve, delegate, commercialize, pause or retire. 6. Arrange the actual steward, resources and delivery. Verify the delivery where it is part of the commitment. 7. Return use, corrections, failures and changed conditions to the shared understanding. A result can remain useful after the original pursuit changes. It can also stop deserving continued effort. Its value and obligations determine what follows.

labels.practiceIntro: You can work with the drill example or a result you know. Choose what should happen to it, who will maintain it, what they need, and how people will get it. Decide what feedback would make you reconsider. Saving is optional.
labels.resultLabel: Which result are you considering, and who could it help?
labels.stewardLabel: Who agreed to maintain it, with what resources, and how will people get it?
labels.feedbackLabel: What use, correction, failure, or changed condition should prompt another look?

steps.label: Support
steps.source: Establish what is supported and whose situation it can help.
steps.prompt: Name the finding or method, the evidence behind it, and the people or conditions it may fit.
steps.check: Keep the supported result distinct from a promise that it will work everywhere.

steps.label: Access
steps.source: Research existing ways to provide access and people or systems that could maintain it.
steps.prompt: Look for adequate existing resources, delivery routes, and people or systems able to maintain the result.
steps.check: Name a real route and potential steward; a label or intention is not an operator.

steps.label: Benefit and burden
steps.source: Compare the added benefit and total burden of candidate forms.
steps.prompt: Compare what each candidate adds with the time, resources, maintenance, and obligations it creates.
steps.check: Compare options over the same intended use and conditions.

steps.label: Economics
steps.source: Examine exchange and economics when commercialization is proposed.
steps.prompt: If considering a commercial arrangement, examine what is exchanged and whether delivery can be supported.
steps.check: Commercialization is one possible disposition, not a required next step.

steps.label: Disposition
steps.source: Choose retain, share, recommend, improve, delegate, commercialize, pause or retire.
steps.prompt: Choose the form that fits the supported use, available alternatives, burden, and ownership.
steps.check: Use the choices below to inspect the practical commitment each option implies.

steps.label: Delivery
steps.source: Arrange the actual steward, resources and delivery; check committed delivery.
steps.prompt: Name who accepted responsibility, what resources they can use, and how the result reaches its users.
steps.check: Verify a committed delivery from evidence that it happened, not from preparation or a plan.

steps.label: Feedback
steps.source: Return use, corrections, failures and changed conditions to shared understanding.
steps.prompt: Decide how actual use, corrections, failures, and changed conditions will reach the people able to act.
steps.check: Revisit the disposition when relevance or burden changes.

dispositions.label: Retain
dispositions.description: Keep it available within a stated scope; name the owner and review condition.

dispositions.label: Share
dispositions.description: Give the intended users access and state what the shared result does not promise.

dispositions.label: Recommend
dispositions.description: Point people to an adequate existing resource when a duplicate adds little.

dispositions.label: Improve
dispositions.description: Make a bounded change for a supported need and name who can maintain it.

dispositions.label: Delegate
dispositions.description: Transfer responsibility only to a steward who accepts it with usable resources.

dispositions.label: Commercialize
dispositions.description: Use only when exchange, economics, operator, resources, and delivery support the offer.

dispositions.label: Pause
dispositions.description: State what stops, what remains available, and what would prompt review.

dispositions.label: Retire
dispositions.description: End continued operation responsibly; consider users who need notice or a transition.
